chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:

Zurarah asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about salat (prayer) in fox, fennec, squirrel, and other furs. So he brought out a book which he stated was dictated by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم:

Indeed, salat (prayer) in the fur of every thing whose eating is forbidden is invalid; so salat (prayer) in its fur, hair, skin, urine, dung, and everything from it is invalid. That salat (prayer) is not accepted until he prays in something other than it, from what Allah has made lawful to eat.

Then he said: O Zurarah, this is from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, so preserve that, O Zurarah. If it is from that whose flesh is eaten, then salat (prayer) in its fur, urine, hair, dung, milk, and everything from it is permissible, when you know that it is properly slaughtered and that slaughter has purified it. But if it is other than that, from what you have been prohibited from eating or what has been made forbidden for you to eat, then salat (prayer) in everything from it is invalid, whether slaughter has purified it or it has not been purified.

key_terms.الذَّبْحُ: slaughter, the lawful act by which the animal is rendered fit
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الْوَبَرِ: fur or soft animal hair used in garments or coverings
key_terms.جَائِزَةٌ: permissible or valid, describing the ruling of the salat (prayer)
key_terms.حَرَامٍ: forbidden, describing animals whose flesh may not be eaten
key_terms.ذَكِيٌّ: properly slaughtered according to the law
key_terms.لَا تُقْبَلُ: not accepted, indicating invalidity of the salat (prayer)
key_terms.يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ: whose flesh is eaten, meaning an animal lawful for consumption

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) valid in clothing made from the fur or skin of animals that are haram to eat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on salat (prayer) with garments or materials taken from animals. It states that prayer is invalid in anything derived from animals whose flesh is haram to eat, while prayer in products of animals whose flesh is halal is permissible if the animal was properly slaughtered. The report also attributes this ruling to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
